text: A dashboard that shows a procurement clerk the entire company's payroll journal isn't a reporting success, it's a security incident. Before you build or run a single report, you need to understand how Oracle Fusion decides who sees what.

There are two independent layers. Function security asks: can this user even open this tool or this content at all? That's governed by duty roles. Data security asks a separate question: given that they can open it, which rows of data are they actually allowed to see? That's governed by data access sets tied to ledgers and business units. A user can have one without the other.

Duty roles control the catalog. A Payables-focused role grants the Payables subject area in OTBI, not General Ledger automatically. Separate duty roles control who can open the Financial Reporting Center, and who can author versus simply run a BI Publisher report.

Data security filters rows, not menus. The same OTBI analysis, run by two different users, can legitimately return two different result sets, because each user's data access set scopes it differently. So if a client says a report's numbers look wrong, check their data access scope before assuming the report is broken.

Here's the key design point: all four tools, OTBI, BI Publisher, Financial Reporting Studio, and Smart View, sit on the exact same security model as the transactional work areas. If you can't see Payables invoices in Payables, you can't see them in an OTBI analysis either. That closes out Chapter 1. Up next, Chapter 2 begins with a tour of the Financial Reporting Center itself.
